subject.title: [Feature Request] Add config encryption for credentials at rest

question: Which credential-at-rest model should OpenClaw adopt for stored gateway, channel, and provider secrets: native OS keychain, master-passphrase sealing, SecretRef-only migration, or another security-approved design?
rationale: The source boundary is clear, but choosing the permanent model affects key custody, unattended startup, migration, recovery, rotation, and auth-provider compatibility, so automation should not choose it without maintainer/security intent.

options.title: Design native encrypted credential storage
options.body: Define a keychain or passphrase-backed storage model with doctor migration, recovery behavior, rotation guidance, and coverage for config plus SQLite auth profiles.

options.title: Keep SecretRefs as mitigation
options.body: Explicitly decide that transparent encryption at rest is out of scope and narrow this issue to docs, audit, and SecretRef migration guidance.

options.title: Use partial sealing as a stepping stone
options.body: Revive a limited auth-store sealing path only as an intermediate hardening measure while leaving full openclaw.json, backups, SQLite, and migration coverage open.

recommendation.title: Design native encrypted credential storage
recommendation.body: Define a keychain or passphrase-backed storage model with doctor migration, recovery behavior, rotation guidance, and coverage for config plus SQLite auth profiles.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved design crosses the current SQLite auth-profile persistence refactor, security docs, and config/auth compatibility boundary.
